parts.text: Which claim correctly finds the width of Room P along the $15\,\mathrm{m}$ side?

options.text: Width $=54\,\mathrm{m}$, taking the printed area as the width.
Width $=15\,\mathrm{m}$, because $15$ is printed on the long side of the plan.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Mohan's classroom floor plan is a large rectangle $15\,\mathrm{m}$ by $9\,\mathrm{m}$. It is split into Room P and Room Q that share a straight side parallel to the $9\,\mathrm{m}$ sides. Room P has area $54\,\mathrm{m}^{2}$.

part_answers.answer: Room P uses the shared 9 m side as one dimension, so width = area ÷ 9 = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 m.

teacher.key_rationale: Area = length × width with shared side 9 m, so width = 54/9 = 6 m. Taking the area or the printed 15 m as width confuses labels with the missing dimension.
